title: Variance Hotspot Finder and Notification Orchestrator for Usage/Cost/Latency
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Problem: Short-duration high-impact deviations (spikes or drops) in token usage, billing spikes, and tail latency are often lost in aggregate alerts or buried by noisy detectors. We need a backend pipeline + orchestrator that detects variance 'hotspots' across dimensions (customer, route, region, model, deployment tier), computes a compact attribution, and then makes a notification decision that balances noise, operational cost, and customer impact.

Goal: Implement a Variance Hotspot Finder (VHF) that complements existing anomaly systems by focusing on transient, high-variance events and an accompanying Notification Orchestrator that applies adaptive suppression, routing, and escalation rules. The feature should integrate with the Console (dashboards, per-route timelines), existing telemetry storage, and Pager/Slack routing.

Success metric: reduction in missed high-impact events (precision at detecting top-5% cost/latency excursions) and 30% fewer false-positive pages for on-call teams during trial cohort.
acceptance_criteria: VHF ingests usage/cost/latency timeseries (per-tenant, per-route, per-region) and computes variance and entropy metrics over configurable windows (1m/5m/1h)

Hotspots are scored and ranked; top-N hotspots emitted to downstream topic with attribution fields: primary dimension, secondary dimension, relative magnitude, estimated cost impact, and sample traces/requests
Notification Orchestrator implements adaptive suppression: historical-noise-aware cooldowns, dynamic thresholds for busy windows, and per-customer sensitivity overrides
Routing rules deliver notifications to the correct escalation target (SRE, Billing Ops, Product) with a tailored message template and links to the Console hotspot view
End-to-end tests that simulate synthetic spikes and verify detection + routing within SLA (<= 90s for 1m window anomalies)
Dashboard panel in Console that visualizes variance hotspots and allows manual mute/unmute and tune of sensitivity per namespace
technical_notes: Algorithm: compute rolling variance, coefficient of variation (CV), and sample entropy per timeseries. Combine with a burstiness factor (second derivative) to prefer sudden excursions over slow drifts.
Aggregation: primary pipelines will roll up at 1m granularity into materialized hourly shards for cost-bound offline analysis; streaming path will use tumbling 1m windows for real-time alerts.

Attribution: use correlated delta scoring across dimensions (route, model, region, instance) and lightweight causal heuristics (request-path sampling + header enrichment) to suggest the likely root domain.
Storage: hotspot records written to kafka topic 'vhf-hotspots' and short-lived hotspot cache in Redis keyed by tenant+route to support suppression logic.
Compute: implement detector as a new Flink job (or kstreams prototype) co-located in analytics cluster; provide CPU/GPU-less implementation to minimize cost.
Backwards compatibility: detectors must not replace existing anomaly pipeline; emit a compatibility flag so Console can display both signals side-by-side.
Privacy: do not include raw request bodies in hotspot payloads; only include example request header hashes and sampling IDs.
telemetry_queries:
-- Example: 1m rolling CV for route="/v1/generate"
SELECT tenant_id, route, time_bucket('1 minute', ts) as minute, stddev_pop(tokens)/nullif(avg(tokens),0) as cv FROM token_usage WHERE ts >= now() - interval '2 hours' GROUP BY tenant_id, route, minute ORDER BY cv DESC LIMIT 100;

-- Example: detect sudden cost delta by tenant
SELECT tenant_id, minute, total_cost, LAG(total_cost) OVER (PARTITION BY tenant_id ORDER BY minute) as prev_cost, (total_cost - prev_cost)/nullif(prev_cost,1) as pct_delta FROM cost_rollups WHERE minute >= now() - interval '6 hours' HAVING pct_delta > 0.5;

-- PromQL-style for latency tail
histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le,tenant,route))
-- Hotspot output schema (Kafka JSON): tenant_id, route, region, window_start, window_end, score, score_components (cv,entropy,burst), estimated_cost_delta, sample_trace_ids
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): enable VHF for 5 pilot tenants (billing, core-prod, analytics) behind feature flag vhf.canary; only emit to internal Slack channel #vhf-canary
Phase 2 (wider beta): enable for 20% of tenants with opt-in via Console; add routing to PagerDuty escalation policy 'Console-Metrics-P1'
Phase 3 (GA): enable default detection at low sensitivity for all tenants; allow tenant admins to tune sensitivity and mute rules in Console
Feature flags: vhf.enabled, vhf.sample_rate, vhf.sensitivity.default, vhf.per_tenant_override
Rollback criteria: false positives rate > 40% in canary window OR > 3 escalations in same on-call shift triggered by VHF
